✅ **Ewing sarcoma of the left femur**, clinical stage IIB (localized, high-grade, >8 cm or involving major vessels/nerves — pending MRI).  
⚠️ Differential includes: Chronic bacterial osteomyelitis, osteosarcoma (less likely given small round blue cell histology), lymphoma, or Langerhans cell histiocytosis.

This 13-year-old male presents with a classic triad for Ewing sarcoma: (1) age-appropriate (peak incidence 10–20 years), (2) progressive, activity- and night-aggravated bone pain without systemic inflammatory signs (no fever, normal WBC, but *disproportionately elevated ESR* — a known paraneoplastic feature in Ewing), and (3) radiographic findings of **lytic diaphyseal lesions with laminated ("onion-skin") periosteal reaction**, highly specific for Ewing sarcoma or chronic osteomyelitis. The biopsy finding of **small round blue cells** strongly favors Ewing sarcoma over osteosarcoma (which shows malignant osteoid production) or LCH (which shows CD1a+/S100+ histiocytes). While lymphoma and rhabdomyosarcoma are in the differential, the *diaphyseal location*, *periosteal reaction*, and *absence of lymphadenopathy or soft-tissue mass on initial imaging* make them less likely. [DIAGNOSIS]  
Ewing sarcoma
